title: Air Canada Express 8646
summary: On 22 March 2026, a Bombardier CRJ900 operating Air Canada Express Flight 8646 collided with an Oshkosh Striker 1500 aircraft rescue firefighting vehicle (R35) on runway 4 at LaGuardia Airport while landing. The ATC local controller cleared the firefighting truck to cross an active landing runway without verifying that the runway was clear of landing traffic. The aircraft was on short final approach at an altitude of 130 feet when the clearance was issued, approximately 4,400 feet from the runway crossing point. The collision destroyed the aircraft's cockpit, killing both pilots. A flight attendant seated in a jump seat near the cockpit was ejected and injured.
probable_cause: The air traffic control local controller cleared the aircraft rescue firefighting vehicle (R35) and other vehicles to cross runway 4 without verifying that the runway was clear of landing traffic. The controller issued the clearance when Jazz flight 646 was on a short final approach at 130 feet above ground level, approximately 4,400 feet away from the point where the vehicles were directed to cross. Contributing to the accident were the failure of the Airport Surface Detection Equipment (ASDE-X) system to detect and alert the controller of the runway conflict, due to the absence of transponders on the ground response vehicles, and the early extinguishment of the runway entrance lights (RELs) before the aircraft reached the taxiway D and runway 4 intersection.

factors.evidence: ATC local controller instructed R35 and company to cross runway 4 at taxiway D at 23:37:04 when aircraft was 4,400 feet away on short final at 130 feet altitude (p. 4). Controller issued clearance without verifying runway was clear of landing traffic.

R35 vehicle crossed onto runway 4 while aircraft was landing. Vehicle reached runway edge and entered runway after controller's second stop instruction at 23:37:20 but continued into runway at 23:37:22 (p. 5).

ASDE-X system did not generate alert for runway conflict. Multiple ground vehicles had no transponders; system displayed only two radar targets instead of all seven response vehicles, unable to establish high-confidence tracks or predict conflict (p. 11-12).

Aircraft struck rear-right side of R35 at intersection of taxiway D and runway 4 at 23:37:23 with aircraft ground speed of 90 knots (p. 5). Collision destroyed cockpit and forward fuselage, killing both pilots.

Night visual meteorological conditions prevailed. At time of accident, visibility was 4 statute miles in light rain and mist (p. 14). Weather observation at 22:51 showed visibility 7 miles; next observation at 23:51 showed 4 miles.

events.text: ATC local controller cleared Jazz flight 646 to land on runway 4
R35 (Rescue 35) and six other response vehicles departed fire station to respond to emergency near terminal B
Tool Truck 7 attempted radio call to ATC (obscured by simultaneous transmission) and coordinated with R35; R35 entered taxiway BB
Tool Truck 7 retried radio contact and coordinated with R35 to contact tower
ATC asked which vehicle needed to cross a runway; R35 moved to front of waiting vehicles at taxiway BB and D intersection
Red runway entrance lights (RELs) illuminated at taxiway D and runway 4 intersection to warn of landing aircraft
R35 crew replied to ATC acknowledgement and requested clearance to cross runway 4 at taxiway D
ATC local controller instructed R35 and company to cross runway 4 at taxiway D
R35 crew read back clearance and began moving along taxiway D toward runway 4
ATC local controller immediately instructed R35 to stop after giving taxiing instruction to another airplane
Aircraft main landing gear touched down approximately 1,450 feet from taxiway D; control transferred from first officer to captain
ATC ordered R35 to stop again; aircraft applied brakes and deployed thrust reversers
Red runway entrance lights extinguished as aircraft progressed down runway
Aircraft nose landing gear touched down; R35 vehicle entering runway 4 at approximately 30 mph
Collision: Aircraft struck rear-right side of R35 at intersection of taxiway D and runway 4 with ground speed of 90 knots
